Festivals · July · Central

Bakatue

Elmina opens its lagoon

Bakatue, Fante for “the opening of the lagoon”, is the July festival of Elmina in the Central Region. After six sacred weeks with fishing banned in the Benya lagoon, the paramount chief casts a ceremonial net into the water three times on the first Tuesday of July, the ban is lifted, and there is a regatta. A grand durbar at Elmina Castle follows on the Saturday.

First Tuesday of JulyBe at the Benya lagoon for the net casting, then come back on Saturday for the durbar.

When
The first Tuesday of July; durbar on the Saturday
Where
The Benya lagoon and Elmina Castle, Elmina
Kept by
The chiefs and people of the Edina Traditional Area, led by the Edinamanhen
Before it
Six sacred weeks with fishing in the lagoon banned
Region
Central

The sacred weeks and the opening

  1. Early June

    Six sacred weeks begin

    Fishing in the lagoon and noise-making are banned. Fresh farm produce may not be sold in Elmina and fish only at the landing beaches; the bereaved may not wail, and anyone who dies is buried the same day.2

  2. Three weeks before

    A fast for the gods

    A holy wooden platter is turned over to begin a three-week fast for the gods, and priests and priestesses hold sacred drumming and dancing, the Dombo ceremonies.2

  3. First Tuesday of July

    The net is cast

    Chiefs, queen mothers and priests process from the palace to the lagoon. The Edinamanhen offers mashed yam, herbs and eggs to break the gods’ fast, then casts his net three times; each cast brings in fish, and the last is met with gunfire, music and dance.2 The ban is lifted and a regatta follows, with women’s groups out on the water in canoes.12

  4. Saturday

    The durbar

    The festival closes with a grand durbar on the forecourt of Elmina Castle.2

What Bakatue remembers

Bakatue marks the founding of Elmina. One telling has the founder, Kwa Amankwa, finding water at the stream he named Be-enya, and meeting a deity there who stayed for eight days; the festival honours that meeting.3

Good to know if you go

  • Where: the Benya lagoon runs behind Elmina Castle; the net casting is on its banks.
  • Two days to see: the Tuesday for the rites and regatta, the Saturday for the durbar.
  • During the sacred weeks: respect the bans in town, especially on noise.
  • Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
  • In January: Elmina also keeps Edina Bronya.

Questions people ask

What does Bakatue mean?

It is Fante for “the opening of the lagoon”, the Benya lagoon at Elmina.

When is Bakatue?

On the first Tuesday of July, after six sacred weeks, with a grand durbar at Elmina Castle that Saturday.

What happens at Bakatue?

The paramount chief casts a ceremonial net into the lagoon three times to lift the fishing ban, followed by a regatta and a durbar.
